common_name: Captain Rawes Camellia (Original 1820s Rose-Pink Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Captain Rawes was the first Camellia reticulata introduced to Britain in the 1820s from Yunnan, China.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind since reticulata camellias are less cold-hardy than japonica types. Captain Rawes was the first reticulata camellia brought to the West from Yunnan, China in the 1820s, and it remains prized for large, semi-double, rose-pink blooms up to 5-6 inches across on an upright shrub or small tree with distinctively large, matte, leathery leaves that set the species apart from japonica and sasanqua camellias. It grows more openly and slowly than japonica types and blooms in mid-to-late winter into spring. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Crimson Robe Camellia (Large Deep Red Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Crimson Robe is a vigorous, large-flowered reticulata camellia.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Crimson Robe bears large, semi-double to peony-form deep red blooms with prominent golden stamens on a vigorous, upright shrub with the bold, leathery foliage typical of Camellia reticulata. It flowers in mid-to-late winter into spring, growing more openly and slowly than japonica camellias, and its rich color and substantial flower size have made it a long-standing favorite among reticulata collectors. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Purple Gown Camellia (Full Peony-Form Rose-Purple Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Purple Gown is a slow-growing, historic Chinese reticulata camellia cultivar with very full peony-form blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Purple Gown, one of the historic Chinese reticulata cultivars, bears very full, rose-purple peony-form blooms up to 6 inches across, densely packed with irregular petals in a rich, saturated color unusual among camellias. It grows more slowly than most reticulata cultivars, forming a compact, dense shrub over time rather than the open, rangy habit typical of the species. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Buddha Camellia (Giant Loose Peony-Form Rose-Red Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Buddha is a historic Chinese reticulata camellia noted for producing some of the largest flowers of any camellia.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Buddha bears enormous, loose peony-form, rose-red blooms that can reach 7 inches across, among the largest flowers of any camellia, on an open, somewhat sprawling shrub that benefits from staking or support to keep the heavy blooms from weighing branches to the ground. Its sheer flower size makes it a dramatic specimen and exhibition camellia, blooming in mid-to-late winter into spring. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Butterfly Wings Camellia (Ruffled Twisted-Petal Deep Pink Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Butterfly Wings is named for its distinctively ruffled, twisted reticulata camellia petals.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Butterfly Wings is named for its deep pink, semi-double blooms with distinctively ruffled, twisted petals that catch and flutter in a breeze, an unusual texture among reticulata camellias that mostly show smoother, more even petal forms. It grows into an upright, vigorous shrub with the bold, leathery foliage typical of the species, blooming in mid-to-late winter into spring. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Noble Pearl Camellia (Large Coral-Pink Peony-Form Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Noble Pearl is a vigorous, upright reticulata camellia with large coral-pink peony-form blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Noble Pearl bears large, full peony-form blooms in warm coral-pink on a vigorous, upright shrub with the bold, leathery foliage typical of Camellia reticulata, flowering in mid-to-late winter into spring. Its strong, upright growth habit makes it easier to train as a specimen or espalier than some of the more sprawling reticulata cultivars. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Shot Silk Camellia (Satiny Bright Pink Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Shot Silk is a vigorous, willowy reticulata camellia noted for a satiny sheen on its petals.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Shot Silk bears large, semi-double, bright pink blooms with a distinctive satiny, almost iridescent sheen that shifts in appearance depending on the light, a quality that gives the cultivar its name. The vigorous, willowy shrub grows taller and more upright than many other reticulata cultivars, blooming in mid-to-late winter into spring. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Professor Tsai Camellia (Wavy-Petaled Rose-Pink Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Professor Tsai bears semi-double to loose peony-form blooms with distinctively wavy petals.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Professor Tsai bears rose-pink, semi-double to loose peony-form blooms with irregular, wavy petal edges that give the flower a slightly ruffled, informal look on an upright shrub with the bold, leathery foliage typical of Camellia reticulata. It flowers in mid-to-late winter into spring, growing more openly and slowly than japonica camellias. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Willow Wand Camellia (Weeping Narrow-Habit Deep Pink Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Willow Wand is a distinctively narrow, weeping-branched reticulata camellia unlike the typically broad, open habit of the species.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Willow Wand is unusual among reticulata camellias for its narrow, willowy, weeping branch structure, giving the shrub a graceful, arching silhouette quite different from the typically broad, open habit of the species, and bears semi-double, deep pink blooms in mid-to-late winter into spring. Its narrow footprint makes it useful where a tall but space-conscious camellia is needed. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Lasca Beauty Camellia (Giant Light Pink Semi-Double Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Lasca Beauty produces some of the largest flowers of any commonly grown reticulata camellia.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Lasca Beauty bears exceptionally large, light pink, semi-double blooms that can reach 8 inches across, ranking among the biggest flowers of any camellia, on a vigorous, upright shrub with the bold, leathery foliage typical of Camellia reticulata. It flowers in mid-to-late winter into spring and is a favorite exhibition camellia for its sheer flower scale. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Dr. Clifford Parks Camellia (Large Dark Red Reticulata Hybrid Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; this reticulata x japonica hybrid combines large reticulata-type flowers with better cold hardiness than pure reticulata cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade. Dr. Clifford Parks is a reticulata-japonica hybrid bred to combine the huge, dramatic semi-double dark red blooms characteristic of reticulata camellias with the improved cold hardiness of japonica parentage, making it a practical choice for gardeners who want reticulata-scale flowers in a climate too cold for pure reticulata cultivars. It grows into a vigorous, upright shrub and flowers in winter into early spring. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Valentine Day Camellia (Clear Pink Formal Double Reticulata Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; this reticulata-japonica hybrid, bred by Howard Asper, is prized for exceptionally long-lasting formal double blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind. Valentine Day bears clear, formal double to peony-form pink blooms, bred by Howard Asper from reticulata and japonica parentage, and is especially valued among exhibition growers for flowers that hold their perfect form for weeks on the plant, longer than most camellias. It grows into an upright shrub and flowers in winter into early spring. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately after flowering ends, since next year's buds set on the current year's growth.
